Every inference tool from Act 2 --- bootstrap, permutation tests, hypothesis tests, multiple testing corrections --- also works for classification. This optional chapter applies those tools to classification problems, reinforcing the ideas from Chapters 8--12 in a new context.

::: {.callout-note}
## Optional chapter

This chapter is not covered in lecture. It serves as review and self-assessment: work through it if you want to solidify your understanding of Act 2 tools, or skip it if you feel confident.
:::

## Bootstrap confidence interval for AUC

*How uncertain is your classifier's performance?*

<!-- Bootstrap the AUC of a logistic regression model. Resample with replacement, refit, compute AUC, repeat 1000×, take percentiles. Shows that bootstrap works for any statistic, not just means. -->

## Permutation test: does the classifier beat random guessing?

*Is this model actually better than flipping a coin?*

<!-- Shuffle true labels, recompute accuracy (or AUC), repeat 10,000×. How often does the shuffled version beat the real model? This is the permutation test applied to classification. -->

## Hypothesis test on logistic regression coefficients

*Which features actually matter?*

<!-- Reinforces Lec 12 odds ratios. Test H₀: βⱼ = 0 using the z-statistic. Construct CI on βⱼ, then exponentiate to get CI on odds ratio. -->

## Multiple testing in feature selection

*With 50 features, how many "significant" ones are real?*

<!-- Test 50 features individually for association with the outcome. At p < 0.05, expect ~2.5 false positives. Apply Bonferroni and BH. Show that most "discoveries" evaporate. -->

## Confounding in classification

*Simpson's paradox for logistic regression*

<!-- Age predicts churn (strong univariate effect). But age is confounded with tenure. Fit univariate vs multivariate logistic regression — watch the age coefficient shrink or flip sign. Same lesson as Lec 11 (Simpson's paradox), new domain. -->
